newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan shares end higher as tea firms chased.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan shares end higher as tea firms chased.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on Thursday as local investors went on a buying spree to snap up tea-related shares on Thursday, brokers said.
The all share index ended at 568.9, up 4.2 points.
"Not much plantation stocks are held by the public. Most of them are with underwriters," a broker at C.T. Smith said. "Its one of the reasons why the stocks soar when there's demand."

Underwriters had to pick up shares of the six plantation firms when they fared on debut on the Colombo Stock Exchange in 1995. "Now underwriters may be looking to sell at a higher level," the C.T. Smith broker said.

Bogawantalawa Plantations rose five rupees to 27 rupees and Agalawatte rose 1.25 rupee to 23.25 rupees. Tea Smallholder Factories, which process leaf provided by small-scale cultivators, rose 75 cents to 20.25 rupees.
Trunover dropped to 11.8 million rupees from Wednesday's 36 million as only limited numbers of shares were available for plantaion firms.
